texts.preamble: In Mvc Shri Sathish B.C vs In Both 1.Smt.Kamalamma on 24 April, 2019 In The Court Of Iii Addl. Judge And Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bangalore.(Scch-18) Dated This The 24Th Day Of April 2019 Present: Shri Mahantesh S.Dargad B.Sc., Ll.B., Iii Addl. Judge & Member, Mact. Court Of Small Causes, Bengaluru. M.V.C.No.862/2018 & 863/2018 Petitioner in Mvc Shri Sathish B.C., 862/2018 Son of Chikka Madde Gowda, Aged about 26 years, Residing at No.708, 2nd Main Road, Manjunathanagar, Dodda Gowdanapalya, Bengaluru-560 061. (By Pleader Shri K.Venkata) Petitioner in Mvc Smt.Madhushree, 863/2018 Wife of Sathisha B.C., Aged bout 23 years, Residing at No.708, 2nd Main Road, Manjunathanagar, Dodda Gowdanapalya, Bengaluru-560 061. (By Pleader Shri K.Venkata) 2 Scch-18 Mvc 862/2018 & 863/2018 V/s Respondents in both 1.Smt.Kamalamma, the cases Wife of Late Annaiah, Chikkavanahalli, Nugenahalli Hobli, Channarayapatna Taluk, Hassan District. (Rc Owner of Tractor bearing No.KA- 13-Tb-1827) (Exparte) 2. Shri M.Madhu, Son of Dharmaraju, In Mvc Shri Sathish B.C vs In Both 1.Smt.Kamalamma on 24 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112269534/ 1 Residing at No1.3, 1st floor, 3rd cross, 1st main, Hosakerehalli, Bengaluru-560 085. (Rc Owner of Trailer bearing No.KA- 36-Ta-6183) (Exparte) Common Judgment The petitioners have filed these respective claim petitions in Mvc 862/2018 & 663/2018 as against the respondents U/S. 166 of Motor Vehicles Act for seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- and Rs.10,00,000/- each for the injuries sustained by them in a road traffic accident. 3 Scch-18 Mvc 862/2018 & 863/2018 2. All these petitions are arising out of the same accident, hence, these petitions are clubbed and taken together for common discussion. 3. The brief contents of both the petitions are as under: The allegation of the petitioners is that, on 2.8.2017 at about 5.30 p.m. the petitioners were proceeding in a car bearing No.KA-05-AF-0140, the said car was driven by the petitioner in Mvc 862/2018 on the extreme left side of the road, near Bairaveshwaranagar, 4th Main road junction slowly and cautiously by following all the traffic rules and regulations, at that point of time one tractor and trailer bearing No.KA-13-TA-1827 and Ka-36-Ta- 6183 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and safety of others dashed against the petitioners. Due to the said impact, the petitioners fell down and In Mvc Shri Sathish B.C vs In Both 1.Smt.Kamalamma on 24 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112269534/ 2 sustained grievous injuries. Immediately they were shifted to Dhanush Hospital, wherein they were admitted as an inpatient. 4 Scch-18 Mvc 862/2018 & 863/2018 4. The contention of the petitioner in MVC.No.862/2018 is that, he was hale and healthy at the time of accident, aged about 26 years, working as a driver and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month. After the accident, he could not do the work as earlier. 5. The contention of the petitioner in MVC.No.863/2018 is that, she was hale and healthy at the time of accident, aged about 23 years, tailor and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month. Due to the accidental injuries, she could not do the work as earlier. 6. The contention of the petitioners is that, the accident occurred due to the negligent driving of the driver of the tractor and trailer bearing No.KA-13-TA-1827 and Ka-36-Ta-6183. So, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners. Contending the above facts, the petitioners have filed these respective claim petitions and pray to grant for compensation with interest and cost. 5 Scch-18 Mvc 862/2018 & 863/2018 7 . In response to the petition notice, the respondents have not appeared before the court, placed exparte. 8 . In order to prove their case, petitioners in Mvc 862/2018 & 863/2018 are examined as Pw1 and Pw2 got marked To substantiate the said fact the petitioners in both the cases have examined themselves as Pw1 & Pw2 and they have stated in their evidence by reiterating the contents of the petition . Further, in support of their evidence they have produced prosecution papers and marked at Ex.P1 to Ex.P6 such as copy of Fir, Complaint, spot mahazar, sketch, wound certificate of Pw1, Imv report, charge sheet and wound certificate of Pw2. Further he argued that petitioners have proved their case by producing the oral and documentary evidence. Accordingly he prays to allow the petition. 14. On perusal of Ex.P1 complaint, it reveals that complaint has been lodged by the petitioner in Mvc 862/2018 viz., Sathish on 2.8.2017. In addenda of this, in a claim for compensation U/S.166 of Mv Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 Sar (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others In Mvc Shri Sathish B.C vs In Both 1.Smt.Kamalamma on 24 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112269534/ 6 Vs. Satbir and others). 21 . Further contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 26 years, working as a driver and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month. 22. The contention of the petitioner is that, he has spent a sum of Rs.75,000/- towards medical expenses. He has produced the medical bill marked at Ex.P7 to the extent of Rs.50,000/-. 24. Further contention of the petitioner is that the petitioner has Multiple abrasions and lacerations. 32. Further contention of the petitioner is that the petitioner has sustained simple as well as grievous injuries.
